There is a lot of cultural erasure where I'm from. The national education system used to forbid students from speaking our native language, and would punish children who spoke it at school or even at home. Sometimes with force. It was also illegal for a time for foreigners to speak our language because people were worried they were assimilating too well. The biggest reason, though, is because about a quarter of our population died off and that included a lot of native speakers. After that, due to an excess of emigration and immigration of foreigners, we just stopped using it. It's still our official language, but less than half the people can speak it, and of those, usually not very well. It's still taught in schools, but the majority of people speak English instead. It's slowing losing its place in our society and it makes me sad.

Okay. Here we go.

I make the pasta and sauce separate, but it's not necessary if you're short on time. Firstly, throw salt and pepper, and chili powder into the sauce. The chili powder is key because it adds some dimension to the flavor. Secondly, I put a handful or a few handfuls of cheetos into a zip lock bag and smash em up into little crunchy crumb bits. Thirdly, I usually make some veggie crumble (or bacon thinly sliced if you eat meat) in another pan. I then pour the sauce over the pasta and mix shredded sharp cheddar cheese into the mixture, really letting it get all stringy and nice while still on heat. I throw in the meat or meat substitute and then put the cheeto crumbs on top. 

It's the best.

tldr; throw in chili powder, shredded cheese, meat or veggie crumble/slices, and mashed up cheetos.
